g: (inorganic chemistry) Any oxyanion of ytterbium; any salt containing such an anion.
(chemistry) A metallic chemical element with an atomic number of 70.
(inorganic chemistry) Any oxide of ytterbium, but especially the colourless solid Yb₂O₃ (ytterbia)
(mineralogy) A rare, highly radioactive yttrium thorium sorosilicate mineral with conchoidal fracture.
A silvery metallic chemical element with an atomic number of 39, mainly found in combination with lanthanide elements in rare earth minerals.
(inorganic chemistry) A fluoride compound of potassium with the chemical formula YF₃.
(mineralogy) A synthetic mineral used for its special magnetic and optical properties.
(chemistry) A birefringent crystal, typically doped with neodymium and used as a gain medium in solid-state lasers.
(inorganic chemistry) An oxide compound of yttrium with the chemical formula Y₂O₃.
(mineralogy) A rare radioactive uranium-titanium-niobium mineral characterized by its yttrium content, often found in lunar rocks and rare Earth deposits, that belongs to the pyrochlore group.
(mineralogy) A violet-blue mineral, a hydrous fluoride of cerium, yttrium, and calcium.

(mineralogy) An oxide of (primarily) titanium and yttrium, with small to moderate amounts of thorium, uranium, cerium, and calcium substituting for some of the yttrium and traces of iron, tungsten, columbium, and tantalum substituting for some of the titanium.
(mineralogy) A form of fluorite that is rich in yttrium
(mineralogy) A discredited pyrochlore mineral containing niobium, hydrogen, and oxygen.
(mineralogy) A brown or black tantalate of uranium, yttrium, and calcium.
(mineralogy) A rare mineral consisting of calcium, yttrium, magnesium, aluminium, iron, silicon, hydrogen and tungsten.
(bacteriology, genetics) A gene in Bacillus subtilis that codes for a blue light photoreceptor protein (YtvA).
